passage:
Thursday night.

I found the messages at 9:40. I read them three times because my brain kept saying they must belong to someone else. They were Chinmay's. My hands went cold, I felt sick, and for a while I couldn't remember what I'd been doing before I picked up the phone. Who am I, if the person I trusted did this?

I typed a long post and deleted it. I sent nothing to Chinmay's family. I called my friend Tara instead, and she came over with roti and sat with me, not saying much. She said, "This isn't about something you lacked." I don't believe it yet, but I wrote it down.

I'll decide about us when I can think straight. Not tonight.

— Thomas

qa.q: At what time did Thomas find the messages?
What was Thomas feeling after reading the messages, and what shows it?
qa.a: Shock and nausea: cold hands, feeling sick, reading three times because it seemed they belonged to someone else, and asking "Who am I" afterwards.

qa.q: Which choices helped Thomas that night?
qa.a: Deleting the angry post, not contacting Chinmay's family, calling Tara for company, and putting off deciding about the future until calmer.

qa.q: What might Tara's words mean for Thomas over the coming days?
qa.a: Tara's "This isn't about something you lacked" offers a different view than self-blame. Thomas doesn't believe it yet but wrote it down, so it may sink in gradually.

grounding: Shows discovering a partner's infidelity with shock and nausea, not blaming oneself, avoiding public revenge, leaning on a trusted friend and deferring the decision.

passage:
Thursday, 3 am, at my brother's flat

I found the messages tonight. Damini's phone buzzed on the sofa and I saw the name and the words and I knew. Four months. I was sick in the bathroom. My hands are still shaking. I'm Jomon, and I don't know who I am tonight. Nine years together. Was all of it fake?

My first thought was to message him, the other man. To post everything online. To tell her parents at breakfast. I had the phone in my hand.

I put it down. I don't want to do something tonight that I'll regret for years.

This isn't my failing. I keep writing that because part of me wants to find what I did wrong.

I came to my brother's. He made me tea and didn't ask questions. Tomorrow I'll call my friend Sanjay. I'm not deciding anything about the marriage this week. Maybe not this month.

qa.q: How long had the affair been going on?
What was Jomon feeling after finding the messages?
qa.a: Jomon felt shock and nausea, shaken to the core, even asking whether the nine years were fake.

qa.q: What did Jomon choose instead of rash revenge?
qa.a: Jomon put the phone down instead of posting or messaging, went to a brother's flat, planned to call a friend, and delayed decisions until calmer.

qa.q: How does Jomon's brother support Jomon that night?
qa.a: Jomon's brother makes tea and asks no questions, giving quiet, steady support.

grounding: The diary shows a young spouse shocked and sickened by a partner's infidelity, avoiding rash public revenge, leaning on trusted people and delaying decisions.

passage:
Ira: are you awake
Sarika: yes. what happened
Ira: Sumit's been seeing someone. I found the hotel booking. and the messages
Sarika: oh Ira. I'm so sorry
Ira: I feel like I'm going to throw up. I can't breathe properly
Ira: I want to post the messages everywhere. let everyone see who he is
Sarika: I understand why. but please not tonight
Sarika: you'll want to decide what to do when you can think. not now
Ira: what did I do wrong
Sarika: nothing. this is his choice, not your failing
Ira: I don't even know who I am right now
Sarika: I'm coming to get you. stay at mine for a few days
Sarika: bring your charger and your medicines. nothing else matters
Ira: ok
Ira: thank you
Sarika: 15 mins. I'm leaving now

qa.q: What did Ira find besides the messages?
What was Ira feeling after finding out?
qa.a: Ira felt shocked and physically sick, unable to breathe properly, and shaken to the core.

qa.q: How did Sarika help Ira avoid a rash choice?
qa.a: Sarika asked Ira not to post that night, said it wasn't Ira's failing, and came to bring Ira to stay a few days so decisions could wait.

qa.q: How might things be different if Ira had posted the messages that night?
qa.a: Ira might have acted in pain and regretted it later, making a very hard situation even more public and complicated.

grounding: The chat shows a young person who discovers a partner's infidelity, leaning on a trusted friend, avoiding rash public revenge and delaying decisions.
